question.problem:
Find the eigenvectors of the $2\times 2$ matrix $C$ given that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}]C=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the eigenvectors of the $2 \times 2$ matrix $E,$ given that 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14163153/assets/606e05d7ba459b9a5b8e8b85bc4f85795d01d702e53654cfddf19b9816869006.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
Notice that the matrix $[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]$ appears on both sides of the equation. Since this matrix is invertible (its determinant is not zero), left-multiplying the equation by the inverse gives the following expression for $E\mathbin{:}$ 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14163153/assets/f8cae7d0e54817dfb63084e753cf1fe55dc0c76e1169be5a4aa10993674b073e.svg)

Therefore, $E$ is diagonalizable. The eigenvalues of $E$ are $\lambda_1=3$ and $\lambda_2=6$ and the corresponding eigenvectors are the columns of the matrix $P.$ Computing $P,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}P={[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}=\frac{1}{-3}[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3} & 2 \\ \frac{1}{3} & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In conclusion, the corresponding eigenvectors are

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14163153/assets/34d358f9ef01983572da4d16ffbebbe13c6479adaae848d21ff86f5c3750003a.svg)
